Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps — concurrency & rate limits

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on regarding performance and SLOs:

- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 350ms for single-turn customer support completions (avg prompt + generation ~350 tokens).
- Throughput: expected steady-state of ~1200 requests/min across your EU+US traffic, with peaks up to 2,500 req/min during Black Friday experiments.
- Concurrency: your team currently needs ~180 concurrent open connections (parallel requests) to support web websocket streaming and 2xx simultaneous streaming users.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for support chat and agent UI; connection pooling is critical.

Action items I’ll take:
1) Share a short capacity plan (attached) with recommended concurrency and pooling options and the Redwood rate limits we can push for an enterprise commit.
2) Confirm how many connections come from a single IP vs across many front-ends (you mentioned most will be from our hosted service on their cloud).
3) Draft a proposed MXN for dedicated concurrency (if you want a pinned pool) vs hosted fallbacks.

Could you confirm the concurrency breakdown (websocket users vs API-based agents) and whether you require sticky routing (per-user KV caches)? That will affect the recommended pool sizes.

I’ve attached a quick capacity_plan.xlsx and a short Redwood-rate-limits-summary.pdf — both are roughs to start the convo.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@shoplynk.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps — concurrency & rate limits

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. Quick answers:

- Concurrency breakdown: ~70% of peak concurrency comes from browser websocket sessions (end-user chat), roughly 30% from server-to-server API calls (agent automation). So of your 180 concurrent connections estimate, ~126 will be websockets and ~54 server calls.
- Sticky routing: yes, we'd prefer per-user KV cache for faster follow-ups (session affinity matters for response quality).
- IP distribution: traffic is spread across ~5 front-end clusters, not concentrated to a single IP.

On rate limits: we want to avoid 429s under normal operation. For the initial pilot, can Redwood raise per-account concurrent request soft-limits to 250 and sustained rate to 3,000 req/min while we evaluate? We can commit to a 6-month pilot with usage metrics and a path to a reserved-dedicated pool if it looks healthy.

Also — attachment from my side: platform_team_questions.pdf with a few security/compliance asks. I’ll send that separately to Mateo if needed.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Platform Engineering | ShopLynk
priya.menon@shoplynk.com
